title: Deterministic-invoice-line-generation-with-epoched-usage-batching-and-duplicate-suppression
creator: Asha Mohan
description:
Summary: We continue to see invoice variance caused by non-deterministic grouping of sub-minute usage events into invoice lines, combined with late-arriving metering updates and retry storms. This ticket implements an 'epoched' batching layer in the billing export pipeline to produce deterministic invoice line boundaries, a duplicate-suppression pass keyed by (customer_id, epoch_start, meter_key, usage_signature), and a rounding/proration harmonization step to ensure NetSuite export idempotency and stable invoice amounts.

Symptoms observed:
- Customers report small fluctuating invoice amounts across retries and backfills (~$0.50–$12) tied to bursty metering during rate-limit episodes.
- Reconciler dashboards show duplicated export lines when late usage is ingested after an export job already ran for the hour.
- NetSuite import sometimes rejects lines due to zero or negative rounding adjustments produced when proration is applied inconsistently across overlapping windows.

Root cause analysis (summary):
- Current hourly bucketing uses wall-clock windowing with jitter from ingestion order; retries and late-arrival events can shift which hour an event is assigned to.
- The export pipeline dedup key is currently a best-effort composite that doesn't include epoch boundaries or a canonical usage signature; this makes duplicate suppression brittle under parallel retries.
- Proration rounding occurs at different stages (first at per-event attribution, later at export aggregation) causing small deltas to appear on re-exports.

Proposed solution:
1) Introduce an epoching layer: at the meter-aggregation service we will snap usage timestamps to deterministic epochs (60s epoch for standard plans, configurable smaller epoch for sub-minute plans). The epoch assignment will be deterministic based on event.received_at and a stable skew offset per-customer to avoid DST/hour boundary drift.
2) Emit stable_usage_signature per aggregated row: hash(customer_id, epoch_start_unix, plan_id, meter_id, usage_hash_of_sorted-events). This signature travels through the pipeline and is the primary dedupe key for export generation.
3) Rework export dedupe pass: dedupe on (customer_id, epoch_start, stable_usage_signature) with a tombstone TTL of 30 days. Ensure idempotency by writing export-checksum metadata to exports table and using upserts in the NetSuite preparation step.
4) Centralize proration and rounding to a single canonical pass inside the export stage: apply proration at the epoch-aggregation granularity and round tokens/currency only once using banker's rounding to cents and carry-forward remainder allocation to the earliest epoch to keep invoices stable.
5) Add an Export Dry-Run mode and a reconciliation diff generator that computes the delta between current invoice lines and prior exported invoice lines for the same invoice_id window, surfaced in Console and in a nightly Slack report to billing-ops.

Acceptance criteria:
- For a simulated retry storm test (100k events with 3x retries and 5% late arrivals), export diffs are zero for 99.99% of invoices and < $0.10 variance for remaining 0.01% relative to a golden baseline.
- NetSuite imports of generated exports must be idempotent (re-applying same file must be a no-op).
- Reconciler alert rate for duplicate/negative rounding incidents reduced to < 1/month in production after 48 hours of rollout.
- Unit, integration, and chaos tests added; PRs landed with 2+ approvals.

Workplan / Implementation notes:
- Schema changes: Add fields epoch_start_unix, stable_usage_signature, export_checksum to billing_aggregates table (backfill path planned in next bullet).
- Backfill: Create controlled backfill job that re-aggregates 7 days of recent usage into epoched aggregates; mark backfill runs in export metadata; use feature-flag to enable epoched export per-account to stage rollout.
- Backwards compatibility: When feature-flag disabled, fallback to current behaviour. For already-exported invoices, export_idempotency will rely on export_checksum to avoid duplicate NetSuite lines.
- Rollout strategy: Canary to 5 mid-market customers first (billing-ops curated) -> 25 customers -> global. Use shadow exports for remaining customers for 7 days to compare diffs.
- Observability: Add Grafana panels for export_diff_amount_distribution, duplicate_export_rate, late_arrival_rate_by_customer, epoch_backfill_progress. Add PagerDuty rule for duplicate_export_rate > 0.1% over 1h.

Testing & Validation:
- Unit tests for stable_usage_signature determinism across sorting permutations.
- Integration tests: end-to-end local export -> NetSuite-mock ingestion idempotency.
- Chaos tests: simulate ingestion reorder, clock skew (±120s), and duplicated events.
- Dataset tests: run historical 90-day ledger generation in staging and compare to production exports; run reconcilier compare job to ensure export diffs are within acceptance.

Rollout & Rollback:
- Feature flag is customer-scoped. Start with feature-flag off. Enable for canary accounts with shadow exports for 7 days; if diffs > acceptance thresholds, revert flag for that account and investigate. Full rollout after 14-day observation and billing-ops signoff.
- Rollback plan: disable epoched export flag and re-trigger export pipeline to re-emit prior export format using export_checksum to avoid duplicates. If NetSuite import has already occurred, billing-ops will run a corrective reconciliation flow and a support ticket template is documented.
